Roam
Trip Planner

A Java web application for personal travel planning
and travel package administration

text:
Introduce Roam as an academic web development project. The system serves travelers and administrators. Explain that package bookings and payments are demonstrations, while personal planning records persist in the database.

Project sources: README.md
Photo provenance: docs/ASSETS.md. Bundled mountains.jpg is illustrative.
Project purpose

Travel planning often spreads across notes and separate lists.
Roam brings destination choices and trip details into one workspace.
Travelers manage plans, budgets, packing and memories.
Administrators maintain the catalog and handle demo bookings.

Find my perfect trip

Season match: 35 points
Trip type match: 25 points
Estimated cost within budget: 25 points
Suggested duration within two days: 10 points
At least one matching interest: 5 points
The website ranks destinations and returns the top three.
textPreview: Season match: 35 points | Trip type match: 25 points | Estimated cost within budget: 25 points | Suggested duration within two days: 10 p...

text:
This is a transparent rule-based algorithm, not a trained AI model. Cost equals daily destination estimate multiplied by the selected number of days, per person. Interests use case-insensitive activity-text matching. The maximum is 100 points. Estimates exclude travel to the destination.

Personal trip creation

Choose a destination and enter start/end dates.
Specify travelers, preferences and the group budget.
The server validates dates and duration.
One transaction creates the trip, initial itinerary and packing list.
Saved trips connect to their own planning tools.

Explain a transaction: related records succeed together or roll back together if something fails. The generated lists are starting points that travelers can edit. Destination estimates are per person, while entered trip budgets are group totals.

Itinerary and trip lifecycle

View activities in day and time order.
Add, edit or remove activity details.

Cancelled and completed trips become read-only. Shortening a trip is rejected if itinerary entries lie beyond the proposed final day. Changing destinations preserves manually edited itinerary and packing contents, so users should review them afterward. PDF output uses the browser print function.

Make the simulation boundary explicit when presenting. Simulate full payment records only a demonstration receipt. The server calculates totals, preserves booking snapshots and blocks excessive receipts or refunds. No payment gateway is connected.

Project sources: docs/FEATURES.md; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
Technology stack

Interface: HTML, CSS, Bootstrap and vanilla JavaScript
Page rendering: JSP and Jakarta Servlets
Application logic: Java 17 services
Persistence: JDBC, HikariCP and MySQL
Build and runtime: Maven, WAR packaging and Tomcat
Local development: embedded Tomcat and persistent H2
textPreview: Interface: HTML, CSS, Bootstrap and vanilla JavaScript | Page rendering: JSP and Jakarta Servlets | Application logic: Java 17 services |...

text:
Explain the purpose of each layer. Bootstrap supports styling. JavaScript handles browser interactions and JSON requests. Servlets process requests. Services implement rules. JDBC accesses the relational database. The production WAR uses MySQL, while the default local launcher uses H2.

Project sources: pom.xml; README.md; RUN_GUIDE.md
MVC architecture

View
app.jsp, app.js, packages.js and app.css display the website.
Controller
PageController and ApiController handle pages and requests.
Model and services
TripService and PackageService apply business rules.
Database access
Database and DatabaseSession manage JDBC data and sessions.
textPreview: View | app.jsp, app.js, packages.js and app.css display the website. | Controller | PageController and ApiController handle pages and req...

text:
Request journey: the browser sends a same-origin JSON request, ApiController checks session, role and CSRF, the service validates and performs database work, then JSON returns for the browser to render. MVC keeps display, request handling and business logic separate.

Project sources: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; docs/MAINTENANCE.md
Database relationships

A user owns trips, wishlist entries, memories and feedback.
A destination connects to trips, wishlist entries and packages.
A trip contains itinerary entries, expenses and packing items.
A package connects a destination with a hotel and transport.
A booking connects a user to a package and its saved snapshot.
Payment entries belong to a booking.
textPreview: A user owns trips, wishlist entries, memories and feedback. | A destination connects to trips, wishlist entries and packages. | A trip co...

text:
Additional infrastructure tables hold settings, audit events, login attempts, schema versions and web sessions. Relational links support ownership checks and durable history. Memory and feedback operations depend on completed trips.

Project sources: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; src/main/resources/schema.sql; src/main/resources/packages.sql
Security and validation

Salted PBKDF2 hashing protects stored passwords.
Sessions enforce login and current account permissions.
Ownership checks protect private trips, photos and bookings.
CSRF tokens protect writes, and prepared SQL limits injection.
Upload checks normalize photos and strip metadata.
Login and request limits reduce repeated abuse.
textPreview: Salted PBKDF2 hashing protects stored passwords. | Sessions enforce login and current account permissions. | Ownership checks protect pri...

text:
Passwords use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and unique salts. Session IDs rotate after login. Cookies use HttpOnly and SameSite, with Secure under HTTPS deployment. Session expiry is 30 minutes. HTML escaping and a Content Security Policy also protect rendering. These controls reduce risk but do not imply security certification.

Classroom demonstration

1. Start the local server and open the website.
2. Sign in as a traveler and explore a destination.
3. Create a trip and show itinerary, budget and packing.
4. Open packages and demonstrate a simulated booking.
5. Sign in as admin to show catalog and booking controls.

Run start-local.cmd, then open http://127.0.0.1:8080 while the server is running. Prepare separate demo traveler and administrator accounts beforehand. Use a completed sample trip to demonstrate memories and feedback. Avoid changing real user records during the demonstration.

Current scope and future work

Current scope
Persistent personal planning, administrator controls and demo package bookings.

Future work
Real supplier reservations and verified payment integration.
Live prices/weather and email notifications.
Hosted performance testing and broader accessibility review.
textPreview: Current scope | Persistent personal planning, administrator controls and demo package bookings. |  | Future work | Real supplier reservat...

text:
Destination estimates and season suitability are sample/curated content. No live travel provider, real payment gateway or email delivery currently works. Real payments would require signed provider webhooks, transaction identifiers and server-side reconciliation. Hosting configuration does not itself prove a production deployment. Future items are proposals.

Thank you
Questions and demonstration

Closing talking points: Roam demonstrates a complete Java MVC application with relational persistence, two roles, editable planning records and transactional workflows. Be ready to explain rule-based recommendations, group budgets versus per-person prices, booking snapshots and simulated payments.
